parameters.query:
-- Atomically claim a batch of un-extracted news URLs for ONE worker.
-- FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED lets unlimited workers claim in parallel
-- without ever handing the same row to two of them.
UPDATE public.news n
SET status     = 'fetching',
    node_name  = $1,
    claimed_at = now()
FROM (
  SELECT id
  FROM public.news
  WHERE url IS NOT NULL
    AND (status = 'pending' OR status IS NULL)
  ORDER BY rss_id, date
  LIMIT LEAST(GREATEST(COALESCE($2::int, 25), 1), 500)
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
) AS c
WHERE n.id = c.id
RETURNING n.id, n.rss_id, n.title, n.date, n.url;

-- Save one whole worker batch in a single round-trip.
-- $1 = JSON array of {id, status, content}   $2 = node_name
WITH payload AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb)
    AS x(id bigint, status text, content text)
),
ok AS (
  INSERT INTO public.news_content (news_id, description, updated_at)
  SELECT p.id, p.content, now()
  FROM payload p
  WHERE p.status = 'content'
    AND p.content IS NOT NULL
  ON CONFLICT (news_id) DO UPDATE
    SET description = EXCLUDED.description,
        updated_at  = now()
  RETURNING news_id
),
mark_ok AS (
  UPDATE public.news n
  SET status = 'content', node_name = $2, claimed_at = NULL
  FROM ok
  WHERE n.id = ok.news_id
  RETURNING n.id
),
mark_err AS (
  UPDATE public.news n
  SET status = 'error', node_name = $2, claimed_at = NULL
  FROM payload p
  WHERE n.id = p.id
    AND p.status <> 'content'
  RETURNING n.id
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM mark_ok)  AS saved,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM mark_err) AS failed;

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, saved: Number($json.saved || 0), failed: Number($json.failed || 0) }) }}

parameters.query:
-- Upsert the worker heartbeat. The full payload is kept as jsonb so the
-- notebook can add new telemetry fields without a schema change.
INSERT INTO public.worker_status (node_name, worker_type, status, payload, updated_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4::jsonb, now())
ON CONFLICT (node_name) DO UPDATE
SET worker_type = EXCLUDED.worker_type,
    status      = EXCLUDED.status,
    payload     = EXCLUDED.payload,
    updated_at  = now()
RETURNING node_name, status, updated_at;

-- A worker that died (Kaggle session killed, laptop closed) leaves rows
-- stuck in 'fetching'. Put them back in the queue so another worker takes
-- them. Raise the interval if you run a very large BATCH_SIZE.
UPDATE public.news
SET status = 'pending', node_name = NULL, claimed_at = NULL
WHERE status = 'fetching'
  AND claimed_at IS NOT NULL
  AND claimed_at < now() - interval '20 minutes'
RETURNING id;

-- ============================================================
-- Run this ONCE (click "Test step" on this node) before using the API.
-- Everything is IF NOT EXISTS / ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, so it is safe
-- to run again on an existing database.
-- ============================================================

-- Lets the reclaim job find claims abandoned by a crashed worker.
ALTER TABLE public.news ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS claimed_at timestamptz;

-- Keeps the claim query fast as the queue grows.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS news_claim_idx
  ON public.news (rss_id, date)
  WHERE url IS NOT NULL AND (status = 'pending' OR status IS NULL);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS news_fetching_idx
  ON public.news (claimed_at)
  WHERE status = 'fetching';

-- Extracted article bodies (no-op if you already have this table).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.news_content (
  news_id     bigint PRIMARY KEY,
  description text
);
ALTER TABLE public.news_content
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now();

-- Live heartbeat of every connected worker.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.worker_status (
  node_name   text PRIMARY KEY,
  worker_type text,
  status      text,
  payload     jsonb,
  updated_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

parameters.content:
## 1 - GET BATCH
`POST /webhook/content-get-batch`

Body: `{ "batch_size": 60, "node_name": "kaggle-extractor-1" }`

Returns `{ "records": [{id, rss_id, title, date, url}], "count": n }`

Rows flip `pending -> fetching` under `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so **any number of workers can call this at the same time** and never receive the same URL twice.

## 2 - SAVE CONTENT
`POST /webhook/content-save`

Body: `{ "node_name": "...", "results": [ {id, status, content} ] }`

`status` is `content` or `error`.

The whole batch is written in **one** SQL statement: bodies upserted into `news_content`, `news.status` set to `content` / `error`, claim released.

## 3 - WORKER HEARTBEAT
`POST /webhook/content-status`

Upserts `worker_status` (one row per `node_name`, full payload as jsonb).

See every live worker:
`SELECT node_name, status, updated_at FROM worker_status ORDER BY updated_at DESC;`

## 4 - CRASH RECOVERY
Workers die (Kaggle kills sessions). Any claim older than 20 min goes back to `pending`, so no URL is ever lost.

## 5 - SETUP (run once)
Click **Test step** on the node to the right before using the API. Adds `news.claimed_at`, the queue indexes and the `worker_status` table. Safe to re-run.

## AUTH
Every webhook needs the header

`X-API-Key: <your key>`

The key is NOT stored in this file - after importing, set it in the three **Auth -** nodes.

## BEFORE YOU ACTIVATE
Turn OFF the old *content extractor History* workflow - it claims rows from the same queue.
